title: Lutherans with the Reformed: in conversion the will is purely passive
source_text: XXI. Adeoque iidem Confessionis Augustanae Doctores cum Reformatis docent, in hominis conversione voluntatem ejus pure passive se habere, id est, nihil agere, sed solum motum atque actionem Spiritus Sancti in se recipere, quod inter alios sensit ipse Lutherus. Ut loco jam citato agnoscunt iidem Doctores.
pass_a_gloss: XXI. And so the same Doctors of the Augsburg Confession teach with the Reformed, that in the conversion of man his will behaves purely passively, that is, does nothing, but only receives into itself the motion and action of the Holy Spirit, which among others Luther himself held. As in the place already cited the same Doctors acknowledge.
pass_b_english: So the same doctors of the Augsburg Confession teach, with the Reformed, that in a man's conversion his will is purely passive: it does nothing but only receives into itself the motion and action of the Holy Spirit. Luther himself held this, among others, as the same doctors acknowledge in the place already cited.
